authoredSolutions.1: Zener breakdown occurs in a HEAVILY doped p-n junction, where the depletion layer is very NARROW. The strong field across this thin layer frees electrons directly from the covalent bonds (internal field emission). Hence option (B).
authoredSolutions.2: For a Bohr transition the emitted frequency is proportional to the energy gap. Among the options the \(n = 2 \rightarrow n = 1\) transition spans the largest energy difference (levels are most widely spaced at low \(n\)), so it gives the maximum frequency. Hence option (A).
authoredSolutions.9: Reading the circuit, \(A\) and \(\bar{B}\) feed an OR gate whose output is inverted: \(C = \overline{A + \bar{B}}\). By De Morgan's law \(C = \bar{A} \cdot \bar{\bar{B}} = \bar{A} \cdot B\), i.e. an AND gate with the \(A\) input inverted. Hence option (B).
authoredSolutions.6: Statement I is false: a transistor cannot be made by simply connecting two p-n junction diodes back to back, because the base must be a single very thin, lightly-doped region shared by both junctions, which separate diodes cannot provide. Statement II is true. Hence option (A).
authoredSolutions.33: Each salt is identified by its characteristic flame-emission wavelength. Caesium gives the shortest, bluish line (455.5 nm) and rubidium 780.0 nm; assigning each chloride to its line gives \(LiCl\)-(ii), \(NaCl\)-(iv), \(RbCl\)-(iii), \(CsCl\)-(i), which is option (B).
authoredSolutions.36: Markovnikov hydration of an alkyne with \(HgSO_4/H_2SO_4\) gives a ketone; the only exception is acetylene, which gives acetaldehyde. An aldehyde such as propanal (\(CH_3CH_2CHO\)) therefore cannot be prepared this way. Hence option (A).
authoredSolutions.39: Of the listed statements on the Bohr model, only (A) — the electron's kinetic energy is \(\propto Z^2/n^2\) — and (D) are correct; the others do not hold. Hence option (B), (A) and (D) only.
authoredSolutions.40: Matching each drug to its use: Valium is a tranquilizer (iv), Morphine an analgesic (iii), Norethindrone an antifertility drug (i), and Vitamin \(B_{12}\) treats pernicious anaemia (ii). This gives (A)-(iv), (B)-(iii), (C)-(i), (D)-(ii), option (D).
authoredSolutions.44: Only an aromatic primary amine such as aniline forms a stable diazonium salt (at 0-5 \(^\circ\)C) that couples with \(\beta\)-naphthol to give a coloured azo dye; aliphatic diazonium salts are unstable and do not couple. Hence option (C).
authoredSolutions.45: Nitrobenzene is converted to m-dibromobenzene by \(Br_2/Fe\) (bromination at the meta position, as \(-NO_2\) is meta-directing), then \(Sn/HCl\) (reduce \(-NO_2\) to \(-NH_2\)), then \(NaNO_2/HCl\) (diazotisation), then \(CuBr/HBr\) (Sandmeyer replacement of the diazonium group by \(-Br\)). Hence option (D).
authoredSolutions.47: Across the 3d series the density rises to a maximum near copper then dips at zinc, with chromium relatively low: \(Zn (7.14) < Cr (7.19) < Fe (7.87) < Co (8.90) < Cu (8.96)\). Hence the order is \(Zn < Cr < Fe < Co < Cu\), option (D).
authoredSolutions.48: Matching each transformation to its reagent: \(R\text{-COCl} \rightarrow R\text{-CHO}\) is Rosenmund reduction (\(H_2/Pd\text{-}BaSO_4\), ii); \(R\text{-CH}_2\text{COOH} \rightarrow R\text{-CHCl-COOH}\) is the HVZ reaction (\(Cl_2/\)Red P, iv); \(R\text{-CONH}_2 \rightarrow R\text{-NH}_2\) is Hofmann bromamide (\(Br_2/NaOH\), i); \(R\text{-COCH}_3 \rightarrow R\text{-CH}_2\text{CH}_3\) is Clemmensen reduction (\(Zn(Hg)/\)conc. HCl, iii). This gives (a)-(ii), (b)-(iv), (c)-(i), (d)-(iii), option (D).
authoredSolutions.71: By De Morgan, \(\sim[\sim p \land (p \vee q)] = p \vee \sim(p \vee q) = p \vee (\sim p \land \sim q)\), which simplifies by absorption to \(p \vee \sim q\). Hence option (D).
authoredSolutions.73: Substituting the point \(\left( \frac{3\sqrt{3}}{2}, \frac{1}{2} \right)\) and applying the tangency condition, the line \(x + \sqrt{3}y = 2\sqrt{3}\) touches the ellipse \(x^2 + 9y^2 = 9\) there. Hence option (A).
authoredSolutions.75: (A) \((\sim q \land (p \rightarrow q)) \rightarrow \sim p\) is modus tollens, a tautology. (B) \(((p \vee q) \land \sim p) \rightarrow q\) is disjunctive syllogism, also a tautology. Both are tautologies, so option (C).
